page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance from the c2d server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with hyper-threading, 32.0 GB of system memory, and a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed; while large-block read and write memory bandwidths are average, small-block cached read bandwidth is relatively weak. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average throughput, whereas multi-threaded decompression and database operations are weak.

The c2d-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. Due to its weak multi-core scaling and lack of local storage, it is less suited for heavy multi-threaded compilation, ray tracing, or high-throughput database operations. It is best utilized for memory-bound single-threaded applications, text processing, and light text generation tasks using small language models.
